title: After
program_note:
Before emerging from unconsciousness After a truck/bicycle accident, I was dreaming (a dream?  a near-death experience?) in which my soul was rising constantly, endlessly.  Through the clouds, suffused with a diffuse light, slight eddies and occasional changes in cloud density the only indications of distance travelled, I rose, until the clouds and the dream evaporated.

Vague and just barely describable as it was, the dream stayed with me for several weeks.  I conceived this work After a month or so, sketched it out in graphic form about seven months later, and completed composition of the music one month after that.

Although the level of detail in the score is enormous and took another six weeks to completely notate (there are, at times, as many as 40 distinct string parts), in essence the music embodies a fairly simple idea:  three interweaving lines rise endlessly at different rates, somewhat in the manner of a barbershop pole.  At first indistinct, the lines originate in the low basses, obscured by a haze of white noise emerging from the other sections.  By the end the situation is reversed:  the lines dissolve in the upper violins, once again obscured by a haze of white noise from the rest of the orchestra.  Between these two extremes the music comes into sharper focus, forming recognizable harmonies contraposed with solo lines.  The composition is approximately nine minutes long.

This work is dedicated to my wife, Laura R. Lefkowitz, who saw me and supported me through a difficult time, After.

David S. Lefkowitz

Los Angeles, California

20 October, 1997
